fields.reasoning: The finding and the critic are right: internal/api/daemon_settings.go keeps project settings (settingDef.project, ScopeProject) in the project's git config, which is untracked and shared by every worktree of the live repo, so a builder could only satisfy the clause by mutating the live checkout's config and a verifier's result would depend on machine state rather than the commit. Every other acceptance in this change set is a go test or a testscript, which is what a leaf's commit can prove. Moving the check into the ship-local-gate testscript (already in the acceptance, with its hermetic repo and git config per cmd/rhiza/main_test.go) keeps the intent covered: the key exists, is a project setting, defaults empty (so the gate is skipped with none set, as the statement and health-ci-stability's no-local-gate warning require) and is settable to make check. Decision ci-unstable-gate-rules (3) names make check as Rhiza's gate; that value stays the intent, but applying it to this machine's config is a deployment step like other rhiza daemon set calls, not build output.
fields.statement: ship-local-gate's acceptance drops the clause 'in this repo rhiza daemon settings --json lists rhiza.ship.localGate with value make check from the project settings' and checks the setting's definition instead: the ship-local-gate testscript, in its own repo, shows rhiza daemon settings --json listing rhiza.ship.localGate as a project setting with an empty default (source default), and rhiza daemon set rhiza.ship.localGate 'make check' then listing it with value make check from git config. Setting Rhiza's own gate to make check is not part of the leaf's commit: it is an operator step (rhiza daemon set rhiza.ship.localGate 'make check' in the live repo) taken once the change set lands, and the leaf's statement keeps 'make check for Rhiza itself' as the intended value, not as something the build proves.
